card.name: Linking words in time and duration limits
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as until, more, with, for or if that come right before a time limit, a condition or a repeat instruction. They appear in storage, preparation and cooking directions.

modes.label: Storage and use limits
modes.description: The words until, more or if sit before a time or condition for keeping a prepared product.
modes.example: 2°C to 8°C (36°F to 46°F) for no<< more>> than 24 hours prior to use

modes.label: Recipe steps
modes.description: Words like with or for link a cooking action to its repeat or its duration.
modes.example: Transfer beef to large plate. Repeat<< with>> remaining beef and remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable

modes.label: Until a condition
modes.description: The word until introduces an endpoint such as resolution or dissolution.
modes.example: hours 7 to 10 *or<< until>> resolution of neutropenia.

card.writes: No clear link to the promoted tokens, which are family words (hubby, toddler) and Chinese terms; it seems to hold back this family-word reading in instruction text.
card.plain: It marks the little word before a time limit or an end condition in instructions, such as until or no more than.
